answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-sequential compute-proof-work per identity to act as a resilient anchor in the network vine. The verifier enforces this by checking if every hash output matches a unique, ephemeral puzzle task, treating each identity like a delicate velvet seal that must be broken by energy expenditure. While an honest agent pays this base cost once, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, effectively hitting a shifting dune of processing exhaustion. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn.
